paragraphs: Here's what I take from this one, friend. The queen of Sheba heard a report, and she didn't just nod at it. She went and saw for herself, and she said, "not even half was told to me" (1 Kings 10:7). The passage says the whole world came to hear the wisdom that "God had put in his heart" (1 Kings 10:24), so the wisdom was a gift, not something Solomon cooked up himself.

Now look at where she points. With all that gold, all those spices and that whole fancy court in front of her, she says, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel" (1 Kings 10:9). She says He made Solomon king "to carry out justice and righteousness" (1 Kings 10:9). The passage piles up riches and wisdom, and the one who gets the praise is the LORD, which is the right place for it to land, baker.

So here's my big idea. Every good thing you hold, whether it's wisdom, work, or a little extra, comes from God, and it's there to point people back to Him. Go and see for yourself what He has said, because the Word will tell you more than the rumors ever could. And friend, don't let the shine of the gold base fool you. I've got one, and I know exactly who gave it to me.
